collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: "just the right time! Everything's aligning perfectly"
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: Calls handled inconsistently; usually owner or whoever's around picks up, Calls go to voicemail; relies on callers leaving messages, No consistent first-call process (sometimes take details, sometimes book), Missed calls with no voicemail; unclear follow-up

transcript:
User: Oh I LOVE this. Yes. Absolutely. ...Wait, what were we saying? Sorry, yes, go on!
Agent: Love the energy—no worries. Real quick, what made you call in today: did you see an ad, a voicemail from Jay, or were you searching for a way to stop missing calls?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, I think I saw an ad or maybe it was a voicemail? Both are great!
Agent: Got it—ad or a voicemail, makes sense. What about it caught your attention most?
User: Oh, just everything! The energy, the vibe, it was all so exciting! Yes, definitely!
Agent: I love that—“The energy, the vibe, it was all so exciting!” What made you start looking into this right now?
User: Oh, you know, just the right time! Everything's aligning perfectly, don't you think? It's just amazing!
Agent: Totally hear you—when everything’s lining up like that, things move fast. When a call comes in and you’re busy, who’s usually picking up the phone?
User: Oh, it's usually me or sometimes... well, whoever's around! We're all just in sync, you know? It's amazing!
Agent: Got it—so it kind of depends on who’s free in the moment. When nobody can grab it, does it go to voicemail or get missed entirely?
User: That's a great question! I think it just sorts itself out, really. Oh, voicemails are magical, right?
Agent: Mhm—sounds like you’re trusting it to work itself out. Do people usually leave a message, or do they hang up and you never hear from them again?
User: Oh, everyone leaves a message! It's amazing how it all just flows. People are just wonderful, aren't they?
Agent: Got it—so you’re relying on voicemail to catch those. Roughly how many calls a week do you think hit voicemail?
User: Oh, it's hard to say exactly! Maybe a few, maybe more? It all just works out somehow!
Agent: Totally fair—ballpark is fine. What kind of business is this, like what do you guys do?
User: Oh, it's fantastic! We do a bit of everything—consulting, brainstorming, you know, just Wendy's thing. It's amazing!
Agent: Got it—so more of a consulting/brainstorming kind of business. When someone calls in, what do you want to happen on that first call—book something on the calendar, take details and you call them back, or answer questions and route them?
User: Oh, just have them feel amazing! Maybe take details, maybe book? Whatever feels right at the moment!
Agent: Makes sense—right now it’s pretty “in the moment,” so the experience changes call to call. When a great potential client hits voicemail, what do you think happens—do they wait for you, or do they try someone else?
User: Oh, they totally wait! It's all about the connection, you know? They feel it, it's amazing! Yes!
Agent: Got it—so you feel like they’ll stick around because the connection’s strong. Have you ever had someone say, “Hey, I tried calling earlier,” or noticed a missed call where they never left a voicemail?
User: Oh, for sure! They always circle back, you know? It’s like everything works out in the end. Amazing!
Agent: I hear you. Just so we’re not guessing—when you look at your call log, do you see missed calls where there’s no voicemail left?
User: Oh, you know, sometimes I do, sometimes I don't. It's just how it goes, isn't it? Amazing!
Agent: Got it—so there are definitely missed calls with no voicemail, and it’s a little unclear what happens after that. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation to show what that can cost, just based on your ballpark numbers?
User: Oh, sure! That sounds amazing! But numbers, they’re just so fluid, right? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Totally—we’ll keep it super rough. Ballpark, how many calls per week do you think hit voicemail or get missed… would you say 5, 10, or 20?
User: Oh, that's a super question! Probably around... hmm, just whatever the vibe is—could be 5, 10, or 20! Amazing!
Agent: Got it—if you had to pick one so we can run the math, which number feels closest most weeks: 5, 10, or 20?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Let's say 10, but you know, it just flows week to week! Whatever works!
Agent: Perfect—let’s use 10. Of those 10, what percentage do you think would actually book with you if you answered—like 25%, 50%, or 60%?
User: Oh, definitely! Let's go with a big number, like 60%! But really, it's all amazing, you know?
Agent: Got it—60%. And what’s your average value when someone books with you—are we talking $300, $1,000, or $3,000?
User: Oh, that's amazing! It's usually around... hmm, whatever feels right! Could be $300, maybe $3,000? You decide!
Agent: Got it—totally a range. To keep the math honest, which number is closer for you most of the time: $300, $1,000, or $3,000?
User: Oh, they're all amazing options! I think it varies, really. Whatever feels right at the time! Yes, amazing!
Agent: Totally get it. If you had to pick one number that’s closest most weeks so we can finish the math—$300, $1,000, or $3,000?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Let's say $1,000, but you know, it could be more or less. Whatever works!
Agent: Got it—using your numbers, if you booked even 60% of those 10 missed calls, that’s about **$6000 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$25900/mo** over a month. Does that sound about right?
User: Oh, that sounds amazing! Yes, totally! But, you know, wherever it lands, right? It's all just great!
Agent: Got it—so we’re in the right ballpark. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough with Jay so you can see exactly how we stop those missed calls turning into lost revenue… what’s better for you—later today or tomorrow?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, both sound great! Hmm, later today? Or maybe tomorrow? Whatever you think is best!
Agent: Got it—let’s do tomorrow. What time works best for you tomorrow: morning, afternoon, or evening?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, tomorrow is great! Hmm, morning? Or maybe afternoon? Evening could work too! Whatever you think!
Agent: Got it—tomorrow works. Are you thinking **morning**?
User: Oh, morning sounds amazing! But, hmm, maybe afternoon? Or evening works too! Whatever feels right, you know?
Agent: Got it—let’s lock in a morning time. What time tomorrow morning works best for you: 9am, 10am, or 11am?
User: Oh, all those times are amazing! Hmm, 9am sounds good, but maybe 10am? Whatever you think works best!
Agent: Got it—let’s go with **10am**. What’s your first name?
User: Oh, fantastic! Yes, Wendy! But if 10am feels off, maybe 11am? It's all amazing! Whatever you think works!
Agent: Got it, Wendy. And what’s your last name?
User: Oh, yes, Marsh! It's just Wendy Marsh, but you know, W-Marsh Consulting, or just Wendy's thing! Amazing!
Agent: Perfect—Wendy Marsh, W‑Marsh Consulting. And which time zone are you in—Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, Central... or is it Eastern? Whatever you think is best! Time zones are just so fascinating!
Agent: Got it—just to be accurate, what city are you in right now?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Right now? Hmm, could be New York, or maybe Chicago? It all blends together, right? Yes!
Agent: Got it—just to make sure we schedule it correctly, are you on **Eastern time** right now?
User: Oh, that's amazing! Yes, Eastern sounds right, or maybe Central? Whichever works best, really! It's all so exciting!
Agent: I hear you—calendar-wise we do need one. If you look at your phone right now, does it say Eastern (same time as New York) or Central (same time as Chicago)?
